The project utilized a large LinkedIn job dataset and deployed a prototype for interactive recommendations.

title: Job Recommendation System
text:
Problem Statement
Recruiters face challenges when manually reviewing thousands of resumes for job openings. This project aimed to automate the matching process between job seekers and job postings by extracting, cleaning, and comparing skills through text-based vectorization.

title: Job Recommendation System
text:
Tools & Technologies

Python (Pandas, scikit-learn, spaCy)
TF-IDF Vectorization
Cosine Similarity
Word2Vec (for future improvement)
Google Colab (backend)
Bolt & Netlify (prototype deployment)

title: Job Recommendation System
text:
Key Methods & Workflow

Data Collection: Used a Kaggle dataset of 1.3M+ LinkedIn job postings
Preprocessing: Removed nulls, cleaned text, lemmatized skills, removed stopwords
Vectorization: Applied TF-IDF to convert job skills into numerical vectors
Similarity Matching: Used cosine similarity to match resumes with job postings
Deployment: Built and deployed a resume upload prototype on Netlify
Evaluation: Incorporated user feedback and began testing with Word2Vec for semantic improvements

title: Job Recommendation System
text:
Results & Insights

TF-IDF vectorization allowed more accurate skill-weighted matching
Cosine similarity ranked job relevance effectively for uploaded resumes
Initial prototype testing showed success across diverse roles (tech, healthcare, business)
Future improvements include automated job scraping and API integrations

title: Job Recommendation System
text:
Business Value

Saves recruiter time by automatically ranking relevant resumes
Enhances candidate experience with personalized job suggestions
Promotes equitable hiring by relying on skill-based matching

title: Customer Churn Analytics
text: Customer churn is a major challenge in the telecom industry. This project aimed to identify key factors influencing churn and build predictive models that help telecom companies proactively retain high-risk customers. Using a dataset of 1,000 customer records with 10 features, we applied preprocessing and tested five models for performance comparison.

title: Customer Churn Analytics
text: Customer churn is a major challenge in the telecom industry. This project aimed to identify key factors influencing churn and build predictive models that help telecom companies proactively retain high-risk customers. Using a dataset of 1,000 customer records with 10 features, we applied preprocessing and tested five models for performance comparison.

title: Customer Churn Analytics
text:
Problem Statement
Customer attrition directly impacts revenue, customer lifetime value, and market competitiveness. The goal of this project is to build a predictive analytics tool to identify churn risks and generate business insights for intervention.

title: Customer Churn Analytics
text:
Tools & Technologies

Python (Pandas, Scikit-learn, Matplotlib, Seaborn)
Machine Learning: KNN, Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest
Data Preprocessing: One-hot encoding, SMOTE, scaling, threshold optimization

title: Customer Churn Analytics
text:
Key Methods & Workflow

Data Cleaning: Removed missing values and uninformative features (e.g., CustomerID)
Feature Engineering: Encoded categorical variables, created dummies, handled imbalanced classes
Exploratory Analysis: Visualized distributions and correlation with churn
Model Development: Trained and evaluated 5 ML models
Validation: Used cross-validation and threshold tuning for performance robustness

title: Customer Churn Analytics
text:

Random Forest

title: Customer Churn Analytics
text:
Key Findings

Customers with month-to-month contracts and no tech support are more likely to churn
Tenure and MonthlyCharges were strong indicators of loyalty
Preprocessing and balancing were critical to improving model performance

title: Customer Churn Analytics
text:
Business Implications

Telecom companies can use these models to target retention strategies, such as:

Personalized discounts
Upgraded service offerings
Proactive support interventions

title: Customer Churn Analytics
text:
Limitations & Future Work

Dataset was imbalanced (88% churned), which skewed results for certain models
Some models (Decision Tree, Random Forest) may be overfitting to this specific dataset
Recommend gathering more balanced data and deploying ensemble methods in production
